entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
CODESEPARATOR has been explored for its applications in Bitcoin Script, particularly in the context of Lightning Network development. An example script demonstrates the use of CODESEPARATOR within conditional spending, showing a structure involving keys, signature checks, delays using OP_CSV, and branching logic. This construction effectively separates two scripts: one enabling direct validation with sequential signatures from different parties, and another requiring a delay before funds can be spent.
With advancements such as Taproot, these complex script patterns can be streamlined. By leveraging aggregation schemes like MuSig for key combination, and representing conditions through public key tweaks (Q = P + H(P||S2)G, where P is an aggregate of involved keys), it becomes possible to condense multi-branch spending conditions into simpler forms. This eliminates the necessity for explicit script branching or the inclusion of operations like OP_IF or CODESEPARATOR in delayed spend paths.
When the aim is merely to enforce R reuse in signature verification, CODESEPARATOR is not strictly required. Alternative constructions allow for stack manipulations and concatenation operations to achieve the same effect, albeit with slightly larger scripts. The use of CODESEPARATOR, however, can optimize script size by saving a few bytes, which may be beneficial in constrained environments.
A more effective approach involves designing scripts so that only the signature S is provided as input, and the known nonce R is incorporated directly in the script logic. This method allows for shared secrets based on the discrete log of R between cooperating parties. In scenarios where the private key needs to be publicly disclosed, choosing R equal to the generator point G ensures transparency and universal verifiability.
For further discussion and code examples, refer to the original mailing list post available at [https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/pipermail/lightning-dev/2016-March/000455.html](https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/pipermail/lightning-dev/2016-March/000455.html).
